messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike in token verification errors from Okta (jwks 5xx / 403) observed across api-prod-us & api-prod-eu. >500 auth failures in last 5m, rate of 401s affecting login flows and console sessions
julia (oncall): ack. paging eng-sre and auth-service owners. looking now.
rajesh: i'm on auth-service. seeing `invalid_signature` and `jwks_fetch_failure` in the verifier logs. Okta jwks endpoints returning 502/504 intermittently.
liam: @julia do we have fallback jwks cached locally? we ship a short-lived cache in verifier. can flip to local cached keys if remote fails.
julia (oncall): good idea. cassie, can you coordinate a controlled rollout of verifier fallback? want to avoid token validation regressions.
cassie: on it. plan: enable `verifier.jwks_fallback=true` in auth-config in canary (us-west-2) then expand. I'll push a config toggle via SSM param store.
support-bot: Support queue is filling. Customers reporting login failures and 403s on console. Triage notes: major impact for web login and service-to-service token verification.
rajesh: rolling canary to 2 instances now. command: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/auth-verifier JWKS_FALLBACK=true -n prod --record
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout for deployment/auth-verifier (canary) — 2 pods.
liam: also adding retry/backoff when jwks fetch fails. patch ready, will hold off merging until fallback shows improvement.
julia (oncall): good. cassie please monitor error rate and auth success rate. set alerts at 50% reduction goals. escalate to vendor if no improvement in 10m.
cassie: canary is healthy. initial drop in 401s by ~60% on canary subset, expanding to us-east and eu-west.
vendor-okta-agent: Hi team — we've seen increased latencies across jwks endpoints in our telemetry (partial outage impacting edge). Our incident: OKTA-13902. Working on mitigation. ETA unclear. We'll post updates in Okta status page.
rajesh: thanks for confirming. continuing expansion to prod: updating param on param store to `true` across regions. patches queued for staged apply.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout: verifier toggle applied to us-east, eu-west (total 12 pods).
support-bot: sending status update to customers: "We are investigating intermittent login failures; login/console may be degraded. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."
liam: after full rollout to 12 pods, auth failures dropped 85% overall. still seeing occasional spikes tied to jwks fetch timeouts from Okta.
julia (oncall): good progress. next mitigations: 1) increase jwks cache TTL to 15m to ride through flaps, 2) add circuit-breaker for jwks endpoint and fallback to cached keys, 3) temporarily reduce token introspect fanout to avoid amplifying jwks load. Are we comfortable with those?
rajesh: agree. increasing cache TTL now. command: 
```
aws ssm put-parameter --name /prod/auth/jwks_ttl --value 900 --type String --overwrite
```
cassie: circuit-breaker config applied to auth-proxy — will open fallback after 4 consecutive jwks failures.
vendor-okta-agent: Update: we've applied edge routing changes, some improvement observed. Still monitoring. We'll share a post-incident summary once resolved.
liam: We've also enabled `introspect_rate_limit=50/s` per upstream to avoid backpressure to Okta. This reduced retries and smoothed traffic.
support-bot: sent second customer update with mitigation steps and temporary workarounds (clear cache, retry). No SLA violations at this time but close to threshold for some enterprise customers.
julia (oncall): can someone open an incident ticket to escalate to enterprise success for customers seeing console blocks? add affected org IDs from support queue.
cassie: opened ticket #INC-4128 and invited @product + enterprise-success.
rajesh: logs show last 15m: jwks fetch errors down from 520/min to ~12/min. token validation success back to 99.2% from 89%.
julia (oncall): great. please keep monitoring 1h post-mitigation. plan a postmortem and include: root cause timeline, why jwks endpoints degraded, why verification didn't failover earlier, and follow-ups (improved caching, vendor SLA, client-side backoffs).
vendor-okta-agent: We will provide a timeline and affected customers list. Apologies for the impact — we'll coordinate offline for root cause.
liam: one more follow-up: adding a small change to auth library to prefer cached keys when jwks latency >200ms to avoid blocking user auth. will ship as low-risk patch.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled verifier cache-ttl and circuit-breaker configs to all regions — rollout complete.
support-bot: final customer update: "Authentication degraded earlier; mitigation in place. Some users may still see intermittent errors, please retry. We're monitoring." :white_check_mark:
julia (oncall): incident de-escalating. leaving oncall handoff note for next shift. tagging for postmortem owners: @liam (engineer), @cassie (sre), @rajesh (auth).
cassie: agreed. moving to post-incident review. creating follow-up tasks: increase default jwks cache, add vendor SLA check in runbook, and improve runbook step to toggle fallback quicker.
rajesh: closing thread for now. will add logs and graphs to incident doc. thanks team. :pray:
